title: Derived slice adjunction presentations and coherence squares
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal C$ be small categories with Grothendieck topologies $K$ and $J$, let $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be continuous, let $R$ and $S$ be sheaves of commutative rings on them, and let $a:R\to u_*S$ be a sheaf ring map. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with chosen localization universes. Package the total derived module pullback and pushforward with their universal transformations, an adjunction and its normalization on complexes. Package the slice comparison as natural isomorphisms together with the unit and counit equations. These are the existing interfaces of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization, relocated unchanged so independent proof obligations can import them without a cycle. An invertible inverse mate constructs the coherence square by the mate unit and counit identities.

proof.text: The interface declarations are the original definitions and structures, moved without changing their bodies. For ofMate, take the inverse mate of beta under the two adjunctions and use its assumed invertibility to form lambda. Mathlib mateEquiv_counit_symm gives the counit square. Mathlib unit_mateEquiv_symm gives the unit square after composing with the inverse of lambda; functoriality and the hom-inverse identity cancel the added factors.
